sovereign_country.strategic_role: 支持全中文章程、传统华人客群离岸家族信托常驻地

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global Employer of Record and Cross-Border Contractor Payroll

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa (unitary national jurisdiction; offshore international financial services sector administered by the Samoa International Finance Authority)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English Common Law as inherited by the Commonwealth State, coexisting with Samoan custom and usage recognized under the Constitution of the Independent State of Samoa 1960)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus) - in force for Samoa since 13 December 2020
WTO Membership - Samoa acceded on 10 May 2012; most-favoured-nation disciplines protect cross-border EOR and payroll services
Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (MCAA) - Samoa participates for tax transparency and exchange of information
Heritage double taxation relief arrangements with New Zealand and certain Commonwealth states (historical instruments; status must be re-confirmed with the Samoa Ministry of Revenue before closing)
Tax Information Exchange Agreements concluded with OECD member states, supporting withholding-tax clearances for cross-border payroll remittances
No dedicated Samoa-People's Republic of China bilateral investment treaty is currently in force; China-market structuring relies on enforceable commercial contracts and regional trade disciplines

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, as amended by the Money Laundering Prevention (Amendment) Act 2018, together with the Money Laundering Prevention Regulations 2018; International Companies Act 2019 (repealing and replacing the International Companies Act 1987, as amended); Samoa International Finance Authority Act 2015 and SIFA AML/CFT Guidelines for Reporting Entities; Companies Act 2001 for any domestic subsidiary nexus; targeted financial sanctions domestically implemented pursuant to UN Security Council Resolutions 1267, 1373, and 1988, with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit and SIFA acting as AML/CFT supervisors.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the International Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Samoa is a Contracting Party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention); apostilles issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, Samoa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Constitution (Memorandum and Articles of Association) of the International Company, including any supplementary Chinese-script charter name translation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding subscribers and beneficial owners, notarized before a Samoan-commissioned Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade after notarization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and certified extracts of the Register of Directors, Secretary, and Beneficial Owners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered Agent's Consent to Act and Undertaking regarding maintenance of the registered office and custody of the UBO register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Affidavit of Ultimate Beneficial Ownership and Source of Funds / Wealth Declaration for each natural-person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each ultimate beneficial owner, sworn before a Samoan Notary Public or authorized Commissioner for Oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation and ongoing screening of all subscribers, directors, officers, shareholders, and UBOs against the domestic PEP register, OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, and Samoa-specific gazetted designations. Enhanced due diligence is required where any UBO is a foreign or domestic PEP, a close associate or family member of a PEP, or where the EOR payroll flows transact with high-risk jurisdictions. Screening must be refreshed at onboarding, before each material transaction, and annually thereafter; complete CDD files and screening results must be retained by the registered agent for the statutorily prescribed record-keeping period.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - Office of the Registrar of International Companies; applications are submitted through the licensed registered agent's SIFA portal. Domestic company filings are separately administered by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour Business Registries.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: An International Company name must be expressed in Roman/Latin script and must include the suffix 'International Company' or the abbreviation 'I.C.' or 'IC'. A supplementary Chinese-character name may be registered concurrently for trust and marketing purposes, provided it is accompanied by an official Pinyin or Wade-Giles transliteration recorded in the constitution and is not the sole registered name. The name must be distinguishable from all existing Samoan domestic and international entities and must not imply any connection with the Government of Samoa, any foreign government, or a regulated financial activity.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Group (where implying a regulated group structure)
Any word implying ministerial, consular, or sovereign sponsorship
Any name likely to mislead the public or offend public policy or morality
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may, within 14 days of notification, file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar of International Companies stating the grounds of objection, the distinctive element relied upon, and evidence of non-confusion with existing entities. The Registrar must determine the appeal within 10 working days. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may apply for judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa within 30 days of the dismissal decision. In parallel, a new name may be resubmitted through the SIFA portal upon payment of a fresh name reservation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are not permissible for the statutory registered office: the International Company must at all times maintain a physical registered office in Samoa at the premises of its SIFA-licensed registered agent, where the registers and records are held. Operational and back-office substance for this Global EOR platform may be virtual and located abroad. The Samoan International Company should act solely as the contracting and IP-holding vehicle; any direct employment of Samoan-resident employees must be ring-fenced in a separate domestic company registered under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013, and the payroll rails (Local Payroll Direct Debit, Wise) must be structured so that the IC does not carry on money-remittance business without the requisite payment-services authorization.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate quantified risk: approximately 10-15% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection of the IC itself during the first operational year given the low-risk standard AML tier and registered-agent custody model; approximately 25-35% probability of inspection of the licensed registered agent's premises in a routine SIFA/SFIU supervision cycle; materially elevated risk, exceeding 50%, if the entity is flagged in a suspicious transaction report, if EOR payment flows touch sanctioned or higher-risk jurisdictions, or if any UBO is a PEP or subject of adverse media.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987, as amended (Sections 5, 6, 8, 28–32, 49–50) together with the International Companies Regulations 1988; administered alongside the Companies Act 2001 for domestic-license matters.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Registry of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (Form IC-1) with attached Charter and Memorandum of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; share capital is self-determined in the Memorandum and may be issued for consideration other than cash; no escrow, deposit, or capital-preference requirements under the International Companies Act 1987; the company may commence business immediately upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company subscribe for its authorized share capital as set forth in the duly executed Charter and Memorandum of Association filed with the Registrar of International Companies. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company be, and is hereby, established at the address of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa, for the service of process and statutory notices. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the initial Directors and Officers be, and are hereby, appointed with full authority to open bank accounts, appoint the corporate registered agent, execute the employer-of-record service agreements, and file any requisite operating licenses. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the official corporate seal be adopted and all subsequent appointments and resignations be recorded in the registers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a written name-reservation request (Form IC-0) through the licensed Samoa International Registered Agent, together with a name-comparability check against the national companies register; ensure the proposed name contains a suffix such as 'Limited' or 'International Company' and does not imply banking, trust, insurance, or public-offering activity without a separate license. The Registrar issues a reservation certificate valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Completed Form IC-0 Name Reservation Application
Covering letter from the licensed registered agent
Screening declaration confirming no restricted or prohibited words
Due-diligence identification of the intended ultimate beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on the ground of confusing similarity or restricted wording, submit a revised name within the same reservation window, or file a written appeal to the Registrar supported by consent letters of the conflicting entity within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Charter and Memorandum
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent acting for the Registrar of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Charter and Memorandum of Association, stating the company's name, registered office in Samoa, registered agent details, share capital structure (authorized and issued shares), objects clause permitting international business including global employment services, and any limits on the powers of directors. The subscriber (incorporator) executes the document before a notary public or the registered agent; execution pages are witnessed and dated.
required_dossiers: Draft Charter and Memorandum of Association
Subscriber's power of attorney if signing via agent
Certified passport or company extract of the subscriber
Proof of registered agent appointment letter
Notarial or witnessed execution pages
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar notes defective objects clauses or capital provisions, file an amendment of the Charter within 10 business days; the company may adopt the revised Charter with retroactive effect upon re-execution by the subscriber.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent physically or electronically lodges Form IC-1 together with the executed Charter and Memorandum, the registered agent's consent, and the registered office consent. The Registrar validates statutory completeness and checks the share capital and object clauses against the International Companies Act 1987. Certificates are typically issued within 3–5 working days on a standard track.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation
Executed Charter and Memorandum of Association (original or notarized copy)
Consent and appointment of the licensed registered agent
Consent to registered office address
Certified details of the first directors and secretary
Compliance officer risk assessment for the EOR business scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for incompleteness, the agent has 14 days to cure through supplementary filing; further delay results in withdrawal, and fees are retained; re-submission is processed as a fresh application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Registration Fees and Stamp Duty
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Finance (Treasury) and MCIL Cashier Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon provisional approval, settle the official registration fee (approximately USD 150) plus any stamp duty via bank draft payable to the Government of Samoa or electronic transfer referencing the application number; the registered agent obtains the official receipt which must be attached to the file prior to certificate issuance.
required_dossiers: Official application reference number
Bank draft or wire transfer confirmation
Provisional approval letter from the Registrar
MCIL receipt for stamp duty
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is not posted, the application lapses after 30 days; provide proof of payment within 5 days and request reactivation; overpayment is refundable by written application to the Treasury.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Register Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation with the company registration number. The registered agent then opens the statutory registers (members, directors, officers, charges, and beneficial ownership register), issues share certificates to the initial subscriber, and prepares the common seal. The company must file its registered agent and address confirmation in the same transaction.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (issued)
Registrar's file stamp confirming registered office and agent
Share certificates signed by directors
Statutory register books
Common seal adoption record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If certificate particulars contain typographical errors, request correction within 10 days under Section 155 of the Act; any correction is evidenced by a supplemental certificate from the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Governance Filings and Foreign Currency Account Arrangements
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIL Registry, companies' registered agent, and relevant banking institutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File in the register the appointment of directors and officers as resolved by the board, update the beneficial ownership register, and obtain the certificate of good standing. Thereafter, open the operating bank account in Apia or via an international banking partner for payroll settlement in multiple currencies, ensuring compliance with the Central Bank's exchange-control notification for non-resident entities.
required_dossiers: Board resolution appointing directors and officers
Certificate of Good Standing
Bank account opening forms with EOR business narrative
AML/KYC questionnaire for the International Company
Notice of change if any officer details are amended
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If banking institutions require further proof of economic substance, provide the certificate of incorporation, board resolutions, and the employment-licensing plan; if the registry fails to process the officer filing, serve a notice to the Registrar under Section 161 and escalate to the Ministry's review committee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Labour Division, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Private Employment Agency Licence (Recruitment and Placement Permit) issued under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013 (Act No. 14 of 2013), governing employer-of-record services and cross-border contractor payroll administration in Samoa

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Samoa Environmental Protection Agency (SEPA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE); Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration only (Category C – administrative/office use); no full EIA or Environmental Authorization required because the activity is an office-based professional service with no industrial production, no discharge of trade effluent, and no land disturbance; an exemption confirmation may be issued on application where the premises are in an existing commercial building.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater; incidental sanitary wastewater to be compliant with the Samoa Water Resources Management Act 2008 and municipal sewer standards; no VOC-emitting processes, office air quality to align with WHO indoor air guideline limits; electronic and e-waste (computers, servers) disposed of only through SEPA/MNRE-registered recyclers under the Waste Management Act 2010; no hazardous waste generated beyond domestic-type refuse subject to municipal collection.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate and annual inspection by the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) for the registered office premises; building occupancy permit and structural load clearance via PUMA building inspection; workplace health and safety notification to the Samoa Accident Compensation Corporation (SACC) for employer-of-record staff; compliance with the National Building Code and the Occupational Safety and Health provisions of the Accident Compensation Act 1995 as amended; no handling of chemicals, gases, or heavy machinery, so no additional hazardous-installation clearance is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of Samoa, administered by the Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA); official portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Samoa International Company is non-resident and is statutorily exempt from income tax on foreign-source income; no TIN is issued solely for income-tax purposes. If the IC undertakes any taxable VAGST activity within Samoa, it must apply for a VAGST registration number by filing Form VAGST-REG with the SRA, accompanied by the Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, a certified copy of the authorised signatory's passport, and evidence of the registered office in Samoa. Upon approval, the SRA issues a 9-digit TIN-formatted VAGST identifier (WS-XXXX-XXXX).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under Samoan law. An International Company may elect in its Memorandum and Articles to be a tax-exempt international company, entitling it to exemption from Samoan income tax on all non-Samoan-source income and to the absence of stamp duty on instruments relating to its offshore operations. It may also elect to operate as a closed company or a company limited by shares under the Companies Act 2008, but such elections affect corporate governance, not taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) — a VAT-style consumption tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 of taxable supplies in any 12-month period; voluntary registration is permitted for persons whose taxable supplies fall below the threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa has not implemented mandatory real-time e-invoicing or API-based fiscal clearance for services. Registered persons must issue compliant VAGST tax invoices and file returns electronically via the SRA e-filing portal on a monthly or bi-monthly basis. A restricted digital stamping regime applies only to excisable goods such as tobacco and alcohol, not to employer-of-record services. The SRA requires retention of structured digital records for audit verification.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under the VAGST Act 2008 applies to (i) goods physically exported from Samoa, and (ii) services supplied to a non-resident customer located outside Samoa at the time of supply, provided the benefit of the services is enjoyed wholly outside Samoa. For a Global Employer of Record IC, payroll administration, contractor management, and cross-border staffing services rendered to a foreign client qualify for zero-rating when no employment or labour supply occurs inside Samoa; alternatively, such non-resident IC income falls entirely outside Samoan tax jurisdiction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CED) lodged via ASYCUDA World
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill endorsed to the foreign customer
Certificate of Origin and commercial invoice
Foreign-currency sales contract or service agreement
Inward remittance certificate or bank wire credit advice from the foreign recipient
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under the VAGST Act 2008 and the Tax Administration Act 2020, fraudulent zero-rating claims attract a shortfall penalty of up to 200% of the tax avoided, an additional late-payment penalty of 2% per month, and criminal fines of up to WST 100,000 or imprisonment for up to 5 years. The SRA may retrospectively reassess tax-exempt international companies within a 5-year limitation period (unlimited in cases of fraud), clawing back input VAGST credits and re-characterising offshore service income as taxable if the substance of payroll services is performed by employees present in Samoa.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Falefa, Samoa; statutory administrator of the Exchange Control Act 1976, the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007, and the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Samoa accepted IMF Article VIII obligations in 2012, achieving current-account convertibility for service fees, payroll, interest, and dividends. Capital-account transactions (equity injections, intercompany loans, liquidation distributions) remain subject to CBS exchange-control approval through authorized dealers on a case-by-case basis. Profit remittance from a tax-exempt International Company is structurally unrestricted: distributions to non-resident shareholders attract no Samoan withholding tax, and remittance clearance requires a CBS-approved purpose annotation, audited or trial-balance evidence of offshore income, and registered-agent confirmation. The residual constraint is documentary proof of offshore substance; the WST is only partially convertible offshore, with deliverable liquidity concentrated in USD/WST spot via BSP and negligible offshore WST interbank depth for material hedging.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory baseline under CBS Exchange Control Regulations: all export proceeds, including service-export receivables of an EOR platform, must be repatriated through an authorized dealer within 30 days of receipt and, absent a CBS exemption, surrendered and converted into Samoan Tala (WST). The mandatory conversion ratio is 100% for resident exporters. A non-resident Samoa International Company is exempt in practice: proceeds derived exclusively from offshore clients may be retained in foreign currency in offshore or domestic foreign-currency accounts, subject to an annual declaration filed by the licensed registered agent. The 30-day repatriation clock applies only to funds booked into Samoa; the IC must segregate offshore payroll receivables from any on-island receipts to avoid triggering surrender obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) - Samoa's largest commercial bank and principal authorized dealer for USD/WST
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (dual-currency WST/USD) with companion Capital Escrow Account for share-capital warehousing
Operational Account (WST only, limited foreign-currency capability)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for Wise Business multi-currency accounts as the primary payroll disbursement rail, aligned with the target rails 'Local_Payroll_Direct_Debit' and 'Wise'; Medium for Airwallex and Payoneer where the Samoa IC's non-resident status is accepted under enhanced due diligence; Low for pure virtual-account EMIs lacking a CBS correspondent banker or offline conversion capability. Legal constraints: EMIs are not licensed Samoan banks and cannot accept CBS-regulated deposits; funds held are e-money claims without deposit insurance; the Samoa IC must maintain its statutory registered office and licensed registered agent, and a CBS-reporting bank account (BSP recommended) to satisfy beneficial-ownership transparency duties under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007. The robust architecture is an EMI pass-through account for contractor payouts combined with a BSP operational account for statutory fees, exemption administration, and CBS reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted. The International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) requires only a licensed Samoa registered agent and registered office; there is no statutory mandate for directors to appear physically before a Samoan bank. CBS risk-based guidance permits remote onboarding when the licensed registered agent performs face-to-face-equivalent CDD (certified passports, notarized board resolutions, corporate registers) and the bank completes a live video interview with the beneficial owner. Physical presence is effectively mandatory only for a WST-denominated domestic clearing account at NBS or for high-risk jurisdictional profiles; for the global EOR treasury, a BSP operational account can be opened remotely using a certified true copy dossier countersigned by the registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound-outbound flow with no disclosed equity or intercompany loan facility (pass-through transaction profile typical of money remitters)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of non-resident status from the Samoa registered agent; executed intercompany capital or treasury funding agreement; board resolution delegating treasury authority; CBS purpose annotation on each wire; forecast-to-actual payroll reconciliation; master EOR client contract.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value contractor remittances inconsistent with declared payroll (structuring red flag)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Global EOR master service agreement; contractor engagement letters; timesheet and attendance records; monthly payroll registers with remittance-level mapping to employee IDs; anti-money-laundering risk assessment signed by the compliance officer; annual independent audit report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity via trust or nominee layers (Samoa IC reputation overlay)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated register of beneficial owners; redacted trust deed and nominee declaration; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements; certified passport and residential proof for all natural persons holding a 25% or greater economic interest; signed undertaking to notify CBS of any ownership change within 14 days.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: parent holding company initiates SWIFT MT103 (Remittance Information field 70) from its Hong Kong, Singapore, or New York account to the Samoa IC's BSP dual-currency account, referencing (a) IC registration number, (b) purpose code 'SHARECAP' for capital contribution or 'LOANIN' for intercompany debt, (c) registered-agent client reference, and (d) board resolution number. For CBS transparency, capital injections above WST 100,000 equivalent should be pre-flagged via the authorized dealer's CBS Form EC-1 for exchange-control clearance. Verification bundle retained by the bank: share allotment register, board resolution, six-month source-of-funds bank statements of the parent, and a non-resident IC certificate from the registered agent. Client payroll funding must never be tagged as capital injection; it must carry purpose code 'CLIENT/ESCROW PAYROLL' and be isolated in a separate client-money ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 (priority) for contractor payroll at or above USD 5,000 per beneficiary; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707) where the EOR acts as conversion agent for contingent-workforce procurement or vendor onboarding; (3) Samoa domestic direct-debit and RTGS rails for on-island statutory and administrative disbursements (registered-agent fees, CBS levies); (4) Wise mass-payout API for contractor payments below USD 5,000 across 70+ jurisdictions, using the target rail 'Wise'; (5) BSP intra-Pacific transfers for Samoa-adjacent beneficiaries. Each outbound instruction must carry payroll-consistent purpose codes ('SALARY', 'SERVICES') matching the CBS exchange-control documentation file; multi-currency netting is prohibited unless separately recorded as FX contracts.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Offshore USD/WST non-deliverable forwards (NDF) executed with a CBS-approved international bank counterparty, given negligible onshore WST forward liquidity
Deliverable USD/WST spot and outright forward contracts with BSP as authorized dealer, limited tenors and commercial-purpose evidence required
USD/WST cross-currency swap, rare in practice, requires CBS capital-account consent and documented payroll-liability hedge rationale
OTC vanilla USD/WST call or put options, premium denominated in USD, used only for invoice hedging on committed EOR service contracts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Confirmation Statement and Declaration (Form ICC/AR-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry, Labour and Immigration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days of the financial year end, or by the anniversary of incorporation if the company's registered agent has adopted a calendar-year confirmation basis
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of USD 300 plus 10% per month on outstanding annual government fees; failure to file for 6 consecutive months triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution after 12 months.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual International Company Government Renewal Fee Payer Transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: International Companies Office, Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry, Labour and Immigration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of each calendar year based on the company's anniversary of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A surcharge of 20% of the unpaid fee is imposed immediately after the due date; continued non-payment for 90 days results in suspension of corporate privileges and eventual deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit through the licensed Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation must be submitted to the Registered Agent prior to filing the Annual Corporate Confirmation Statement, and within 30 days of any share transfer or beneficial ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or confirm beneficial ownership records is an offence under Samoa's AML/CFT Act, carrying fines up to USD 10,000 and personal liability for directors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Statutory audit is required if the International Company exceeds two of the following three criteria: total assets exceeding WST 3,500,000, gross revenue exceeding WST 6,000,000, or average employees exceeding 25; or if a member holding 10% or more of the share capital requests an audit; or if the company is licensed to conduct banking, trust, or insurance business.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and adopted under Samoa's International Companies Act Accounting Practice Direction; or Samoa International Financial Reporting Standard for Small and Medium-sized Entities (SIFRS for SMEs) for qualifying companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must maintain a register of beneficial owners at the registered office in Samoa. Every share transfer or allotment requires updating the register within 14 days, with an annual confirmation statement to the Registered Agent attesting the accuracy of beneficial ownership details before the Annual Corporate Confirmation Statement is filed. Non-resident shareholders may be named if exempted by the Registrar.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Director and Member Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 4,000 - 9,000 for a standard Global EOR and contractor payroll entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for a Samoa International Company (ICA 1987 full tax exemption); standard Samoa resident company CIT headline rate is 27% under the Income Tax Act 2012
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, vehicle tax, dividend withholding tax, Interest/Royalty withholding tax, and exchange control; the only annual charge is the prescribed IC government fee paid through the licensed registered agent

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No income tax return is filed for an International Company. Mandatory Annual Return (Form AR-IC) filed through the Samoa International Financial Authority (SIFA) e-services portal / Registrar of International Companies module; all filings routed via the licensed Samoa registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual Return is due on or before the anniversary of incorporation every year; the annual government fee must be paid concurrently; arrears accrue monthly surcharges until payment and filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: IC registration number and full legal name
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the SIFA/Registrar assigned number; no Samoan Tax File Number is issued or required for the exempt IC.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Address of Samoa registered office and identity of licensed registered agent
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot self-appoint; a licensed Samoa IC service provider must be named.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, residential/official addresses, share class and shareholding percentages
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All persons may be non-resident; disclose any nominee arrangement and underlying principal in line with SIFA AML directives.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and source-of-funds summary
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident UBOs must provide certified passport copies, proof of residential address and a professional reference; register must stay at the Samoa agent's office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ISIC 7810 – Global Employer of Record, cross-border contractor payroll, HR administration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that no business is transacted with Samoan residents, no Samoa-sourced payroll, and all EOR services are performed outside Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Status declaration as inactive, non-resident, or relevant activity under the Economic Substance Regulations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs with no Samoa CIGA operations mark 'Non-resident' unless the parent group directs EOR activity from Samoa; maintain supporting board minutes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Monthly late-filing surcharge on the annual government fee; automatic late restoration fee if struck off; false declarations attract a fine up to SAT 50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years under the International Companies Act 1987.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions by a Samoa International Company; Samoa domestic statutory rate for ordinary resident companies is 15%
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable to a tax-exempt IC because the Samoan WHT rate is already zero. If the IC were unexpectedly reassessed as a resident trading company, the entity would apply to the Samoa Ministry of Revenue for a Certificate of Residence (TRC) using Form TRC-A, attach the source-country tax authority's confirmation that treaty benefits are claimed, and present the TRC to the payer before distribution; Samoa's treaty network includes Australia, New Zealand, China, Fiji and the UAE.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: IC exemption: 0% statutory and 0% treaty-effective for IP royalties and debt interest. Domestic Samoa contract rates otherwise are 15% for interest, 15% for royalties and 10% for management/technical fees; applicable DTAs generally reduce royalty and interest WHT to 5–10%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory threshold in Samoa and no Local File/Master File obligation for International Companies; the arm's length principle applies only to tax-resident companies under the Income Tax Act 2012, while the IC is outside the charge to Samoan tax.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations apply to ICs carrying on relevant activities, which include headquarters, distribution and service centre, financing and leasing, IP holding, shipping, and banking/insurance. A global EOR and contractor payroll business must file an annual economic substance notification through SIFA; if it claims non-resident status, it must prove that the core income-generating activities are performed outside Samoa. If the EOR platform is managed or directed from Samoa, the IC must maintain adequate physical presence: a local office, full-time employees, proportionate annual expenditure, and board meetings held in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The IC uses its Samoa payroll rail to engage Samoan-resident employees, serves a Samoan end-client, or maintains a physical recruitment office in Apia, violating the non-resident operation restriction in the International Companies Act 1987.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine against the company up to SAT 20,000 and against each officer up to SAT 5,000; compulsory forfeiture of exempt status; the IC is struck off and all Samoan-source income is retroactively taxed at 27%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the IC's unpaid Samoan CIT and PAYE/WHT, may be barred from leaving Samoa via travel-banishment orders, and face prosecution for carrying on prohibited business in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain the beneficial ownership register, omission of suspicious transaction reports on payroll flows, or use of undisclosed nominees to move EOR payroll funds through the IC's Wise/direct-debit rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to SAT 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 14 years under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007; SIFA licence suspension; mandatory deregistration of the IC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the compliance officer face criminal liability, personal asset restraint, travel bans, and disqualification from acting as company officers in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Rendering phantom client payroll invoices to mask profit shifting, artificially routing funds to related parties without any actual employment services, or exercising central management and control in Samoa while claiming non-resident exempt status.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the IC's worldwide EOR service income at 27% CIT with monthly interest; penalty up to 100% of the tax avoided; fine up to SAT 100,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years for tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced for fraudulent or sham transactions; directors must make civil restitution of unpaid tax and interest, may have passports impounded, and are exposed to custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a de facto money remitter by receiving global client payroll funds and disbursing salaries in multiple currencies through the Samoan IC without a Central Bank of Samoa payment-services licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to SAT 500,000 under Samoa's financial institutions law; freezing of the IC's bank accounts; revocation of the IC charter; restitution orders for funds processed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Each director is personally liable for fines, is subject to director-banishment proceedings, and may be disqualified for up to 10 years from managing any Samoa-registered entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Falsified Annual Return / Evasion of Registrar Supervision
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting an annual return declaring nil relevant activity while the IC simultaneously operates a Samoa-staffed EOR centre, misrepresenting the beneficiary owners, or concealing the true payroll volume.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strict liability fine up to SAT 50,000, imprisonment up to 5 years, automatic suspension of the IC's exempt status, and retrospective taxation of all income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed or authorised the false return are personally liable for the fine, civil restitution of escaping fees, travel-ban orders, and criminal imprisonment for perjury-adjacent false declaration.
